item: A law document whose processing raises after a good fetch is stamped like a failed request (check time, error status, 24 h back-off) instead of being re-fetched every pass
summary: track_document stamps last_checked_at before it fetches and commits only on its own return paths, so an exception that escaped it after the fetch (a locked commit, an extractor crash) met the batch trackers' session.rollback(), which discarded the stamp: the document stayed at the head of auto_track_due's least-recently-checked order and was fetched again on every pass with no back-off (measured on main and on the R293 branch alike: 3 requests over 3 passes; with a batch of two, two such documents at the head kept a healthy one behind them from ever being fetched in 3 passes). Now _back_off_after_crash, called by track_watched and auto_track_due after the rollback, stamps the document as a failed request is stamped (last_checked_at = now, last_status = 'error: ...' through record_text, committed), best effort: a failing database or a deleted row is logged and the pass goes on. A deferral, a kill-switch refusal and an error from anywhere before the fetch returned stay unstamped: track_document records on the session (session.info, cleared at the top of every attempt) the id of the document whose fetch returned a result, and the helper stamps only when it matches (a one-off database error reading the document, or a failed commit of a deferral or a refusal, is not a check: R293's rule). A crash makes a request, so it spends the batch: with two crashers ahead of a healthy document and a batch of two, the healthy one is reached on the next pass, not the same one. 8 tests in tests/test_law_crash_backoff.py; 9 mutants caught (helper not called in track_watched, not called in auto_track_due, no commit, no time stamp, no marker check, marker never set, marker not cleared, a failing back-off that raises into the pass). Stated: a crash whose stamp cannot be written is retried next pass as before; a transient crash waits 24 h like a transient request failure.
